solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Lanky drunk crossing hotel? That's unlikely

parts.note: lanky means tall and thin, i.e. long

indicators.note: the drunk is crossing, i.e. lies across, the hotel letter, so it is put around it

parts.note: a drunk is a sot
H is Hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A tall drunk staggering across a hotel lobby is not a likely sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crossing' puts SOT around H.
explanation.definitionFit: A long shot is a bet or attempt with little chance of success, so it is something unlikely.

clue.text: Leaf initially changing daily, covering top of pond?

definitions.text: Leaf initially changing daily, covering top of pond?

indicators.note: the initial letter of the preceding word is taken
the rearranged letters cover, i.e. go around, the next letter
the following word is changed, so its letters are rearranged
in a down clue the top of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A floating leaf drifting a little each day across the surface of a pond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' scrambles DAILY to ILYAD, and 'covering' puts it around P. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A lily pad is the broad floating leaf of a water lily, which spreads over a pond's surface.

clue.text: Spoil piece about old Billy's mate

parts.note: to nanny someone is to pamper or spoil them

indicators.note: the word for piece goes about the other letter

parts.note: piece and gat are both slang for a gun

explanation.surface: A spoilt piece of something about old Billy's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts GAT around O. Billy is the billy goat, not a man.
explanation.definitionFit: A billy goat is a male goat, and its mate is the female, the nanny goat.

clue.text: Martyr succeeded after that, retaining record

parts.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for succeeded

indicators.note: the word for after that keeps the record inside it

parts.note: then means after that
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A martyr's story: he took over, and then kept a record of it.
explanation.walkthrough: S for succeeded comes from family trees, where it marks who followed whom on a throne or title.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Stephen is traditionally the first Christian martyr, stoned to death in Acts.

clue.text: Game individual tucks into out-of-date crackers

parts.note: out-of-date means old

indicators.note: the letter tucks into, i.e. is inserted in, the word for crackers

parts.note: crackers is slang for mad
I, the single person, stands for an individual

explanation.surface: A lone diner tucks into stale Christmas crackers during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' puts I inside MAD.
explanation.definitionFit: Old Maid is a card game in which players try not to be left holding the odd queen.

clue.text: Novelist left under blankets

indicators.note: used as a verb: the word for under covers, so it is wrapped around the other letter

parts.note: under means below

explanation.surface: An author is abandoned beneath bedclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blankets' is a verb here: BELOW wraps around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Saul Bellow was the American author of Herzog and Humboldt's Gift.

clue.text: It's played first of all in dance at a milk bar regularly

indicators.note: that letter goes in the word for dance

parts.note: a ball is a formal dance

indicators.note: the first letter of the following word is taken
taking every other letter, starting with the first, of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A musician plays at a dance held in a milk bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts A (the first letter of 'all') into BALL; 'regularly' takes A, I, K, A from 'a milk bar'.
explanation.definitionFit: The balalaika is a triangular Russian stringed instrument, so it is something played.

clue.text: Butcher's place to go? Try lifting last of pork

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for try lifts, i.e. holds up, the letter above it

parts.note: the loo is the toilet, a place to go

indicators.note: the last letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: to see whether you can is to try

explanation.surface: A butcher's shop with a toilet, and a customer trying to lift the last of the pork.
explanation.walkthrough: Butcher's is Cockney rhyming slang: 'butcher's hook' rhymes with look, so a butcher's is a look.
explanation.definitionFit: A look-see is an informal quick look, which is exactly what a 'butcher's' means in slang.

clue.text: Surgery has problem restraining very big animal

indicators.note: the two pieces hold the other letters between them

parts.note: an op (operation) is surgery
a sum is an arithmetic problem
OS is the clothing abbreviation for outsize

explanation.surface: A vet's surgery has trouble holding down a huge animal.
explanation.walkthrough: OS (outsize) is a clothing-label size, used in crosswords for very big.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is an American marsupial, so it is an animal.

clue.text: Sell iodine compound that keeps bats in good nick

definitions.text: that keeps bats in good nick

indicators.note: a compound is a mixture, so the letters of these two words are mixed into a new order

explanation.surface: A pitch for selling an iodine preparation as a chemical product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like a noun for the chemical, but it is the anagram signal on SELL IODINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket bats made of willow are traditionally rubbed with this oil to stop them drying and cracking.

clue.text: Leader of orchestra regularly broke wind

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
taking every other letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: The orchestra's leader keeps passing wind in performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of 'broke', BOE.
explanation.definitionFit: The oboe is a woodwind instrument, so it can be called a wind in an orchestra.

clue.text: NHS says a policy interfered with a shrink's work

indicators.note: letters that have been interfered with are disturbed, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The health service claims a government policy meddled with a psychiatrist's practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'interfered with' signals an anagram of all fourteen letters of NHS SAYS A POLICY. The NHS is Britain's National Health Service.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrink is slang for a psychiatrist, and psychoanalysis is the treatment such a therapist practises.

clue.text: Saturated Republican put away bottles

indicators.note: used as a verb: the word for put away holds the other letter inside it

parts.note: to put away food or drink is to down it, so downed

explanation.surface: A soaked Republican knocked back several bottles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' is a verb: DOWNED holds R.
explanation.definitionFit: Something drowned has been covered or soaked in liquid, i.e. saturated.

clue.text: English hairstyle I'd adopted is what protects us?

indicators.note: the hairstyle adopts, i.e. takes in, the letters of I'd

parts.note: a perm is a permanent wave hairstyle
taken as written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An Englishman's adopted hairstyle is his protection.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that 'what protects us' is a playful description rather than a dictionary definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The epidermis is the outer layer of skin, a barrier that shields the body.

clue.text: Recoiling, cover heroine's spot

indicators.note: something recoiling springs back, so the word for cover is read backwards

parts.note: a lid is a cover
Emma is the heroine of Jane Austen's novel of that name; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A heroine's blemish is being shielded as she flinches back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spot' looks like a blemish to cover, but it means a tight spot, a predicament. 'Recoiling' applies only to the cover.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in a spot is to be in an awkward predicament, the kind of fix a dilemma puts you in.

clue.text: River shown in diagrams disrupted carnival

indicators.note: the letter is shown inside the rearranged word
the word is disrupted, so its letters are put in a new order

parts.note: R is the map abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: A river appears in diagrams that a carnival has disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disrupted' rearranges DIAGRAMS, and 'shown in' places R within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mardi Gras is the Shrove Tuesday festival celebrated with parades, most famously in New Orleans.

clue.text: Like controversial verses as written about a function

indicators.note: the word for as written goes about, i.e. around, the other letters

parts.note: sic is the Latin note meaning 'thus, as written'
tan (tangent) is a trigonometric function

explanation.surface: A quibble about whether contentious poetry is presented exactly as written around some function.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SIC round ATAN; the 'controversial verses' are Rushdie's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie's novel The Satanic Verses caused worldwide controversy, so the verses in question are satanic ones.

clue.text: Complaint the German's missing problem with train

indicators.note: these letters are missing from the longer word

parts.note: a derailment is a railway accident
der is a German word for the; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: A German passenger complains that a train problem made him miss his connection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' takes DER out of DERAILMENT.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint in the medical sense is an illness, which is what an ailment is.

clue.text: You might pick bird up in this headlight?

indicators.note: picking something up can mean hearing it, so the bird's name is heard
picked up in this word means the word sounds like the bird

parts.note: the oriole is a bird

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher might spot a bird caught in a car's headlight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headlight' is not a lamp but a light around the head.
explanation.definitionFit: An aureole is a halo, a ring of light painted around a saint's head.

clue.text: Marshal stealing Doc Holliday's second adornment

indicators.note: the marshal is stealing, i.e. taking inside himself, the other letters

parts.note: Wyatt Earp was the famous US marshal of Tombstone
Dr is the abbreviation for doctor, so doc

indicators.note: the second letter of the following name is taken

explanation.surface: A Wild West lawman pockets an ornament belonging to his friend Doc Holliday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' takes O from Holliday; Doc Holliday was Wyatt Earp's ally at the OK Corral, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: An eardrop is a pendant earring, a piece of jewellery worn as decoration.

clue.text: Medical speciality doubled European understanding

indicators.note: doubled means the medical speciality is written a second time straight after itself

parts.note: ENT is ear, nose and throat medicine

explanation.surface: A medical speciality redoubles its efforts toward European agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubled' gives the speciality twice, ENTENT, the second copy reusing the same clue words.
explanation.definitionFit: An entente is a friendly agreement between nations, as in the Entente Cordiale.

clue.text: Bring back Danish bread after nap

indicators.note: the Danish money comes after the word for nap

parts.note: a nap is a rest
bread is slang for money, and the øre is a Danish coin

explanation.surface: Bring back Danish pastries after a lie-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Danish bread' suggests a pastry, but bread is money: the øre is a small Danish coin.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore something is to return it to its former state or owner.

clue.text: Put on pressure dealing with nurse

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for pressure
re means concerning or dealing with
to nurse someone is to tend them

explanation.surface: A nurse is put under pressure while dealing with a patient.
explanation.walkthrough: Put on is the verb for faking, as in putting on an act.
explanation.definitionFit: To put on an accent or air is to feign it, i.e. to pretend.

clue.text: Integrate lines mistakenly where colon is found

indicators.note: letters put together mistakenly are in the wrong order, so these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone has wrongly merged lines of text, perhaps around a misplaced punctuation mark.
explanation.walkthrough: The colon looks like the punctuation mark, but it is the part of the bowel.
explanation.definitionFit: The colon is the main part of the large intestine, so that organ is where it is located.

clue.text: Star making a return appearance in Wigmore Hall

indicators.note: a return appearance comes back the other way, so the letters are read backwards
the letters are found inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A celebrated performer comes back for another concert at a London recital venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters ORE H in 'WigmORE Hall' are read backwards. Wigmore Hall is a London concert hall.
explanation.definitionFit: The star of a film or story is its hero, the leading figure.

clue.text: Filling dish, not one intended for rabbits

definitions.meaning: the substantial dish of a meal
a rabbit is slang for a poor or novice player, and a ... (as in golf or racing) is the principal one, not meant for beginners

explanation.surface: A hearty plate that is not lettuce leaves for bunnies.
explanation.walkthrough: Rabbits suggest the animals eating salad, but a rabbit is also a weak player, and the main course is the championship one.
explanation.definitionFit: The main course is the central, most substantial plate of a meal.

clue.text: Fancy woman sacrificing main artery to put weight on!

indicators.note: giving these letters up, so they are taken out of the word

parts.note: a fancy woman is a mistress
the M1 (written MI) is Britain's main north-south motorway, a major artery

explanation.surface: A man's lover gives up something vital in order to gain weight.
explanation.walkthrough: MI stands for the M1, Britain's first and main motorway, a road artery rather than a blood vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: To stress a word or point is to give it emphasis, i.e. to lay weight on it.

clue.text: Delivered grass for planting round fields

indicators.note: the grass is planted round, i.e. placed around, the word for fields

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass
leas are meadows or fields

explanation.surface: A gardener's order: grass seed delivered for sowing around the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delivered' looks like the gardener's order arriving, but it is the definition, in its sense of set free.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone from captivity is to set them free, i.e. release them.
